scope: Isolated native macOS memory-only filesystem feasibility for the App Sandbox worker; not production adoption, a DF-062 PASS or a resource-policy decision
authority: Handoff of 2026-11-01 names this as the next authorized isolated containment task; no new privilege, entitlement, service, VM, transport or tool installation is used
policy_under_test: App Sandbox (standard entitlement only) plus child-local RLIMIT_FSIZE=0 with SIGXFSZ ignored, RLIMIT_CORE=0 and RLIMIT_NPROC=0, installed by the native launcher before exec
independent_observers: FSEvents file-level stream over the task-owned container, with start and end barriers; dropped-event flags fail the run
Host scan of every regular file and extended attribute in the container, without following symlinks
Bounded wait for the ReportCrash report naming the crashed PID
sources_changed_since_previous_manifest: tools/macos_exec_limits_probe.c gained the optional file-growth limit and FSIZE/CORE/SIGXFSZ readback; tools/macos_observer_probe.c gained the growth and growth-launch helper modes; sandbox_darwin_test.go only adopts the launcherLimits signature. The observer-sandbox tests still pass on these sources in the full spike race suite; their committed evidence and manifest were not regenerated and still bind the earlier versions. Condition 3 update: worker main.rs gained the panic hook, read_source.rs the test-only source_panic and source_panic_abort faults, and the memory-only test the panic, panic_abort and crash_trailing scenarios; memory-only-worker.json and fault-seeds.json were regenerated, the other observations still bind 5b434f0 sources SEC-001 update: container.go now sweeps through directory handles (macOS only), container_report.go carries the portable report type, the two flag-helper files were removed, and container_darwin_test.go gained the swap, hard-link, fail-closed and depth tests; memory-only-worker.json and growth-channels.json were regenerated with the same worker, and their sweep counts match the earlier run
worker_build: cargo build --locked --offline --release -p df0-worker with the pinned toolchain and CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repository, after the condition 3 panic hook; condition 1's mapping fix is included
signing: Task-only copies, ad-hoc hardened-runtime signature, only the App Sandbox entitlement; no Developer ID, notarization or installed-app claim. Unique new containers and the task's own crash reports are removed by the tests.
findings: App Sandbox alone lets the worker write file content inside its own container (positive control: 126 DataFusion spill files, sentinel present)
RLIMIT_FSIZE=0 with SIGXFSZ ignored stops file content: write and ftruncate return EFBIG; a forced DataFusion spill fails after creating and removing one empty file

A refused spill write is reported as RESOURCE_LIMIT with a constant detail (owner condition 1). An earlier build reported INPUT_INVALID with the OS error text, because the OS error sits inside an io::Error that io::Error::source() skips
File and directory creation, renames and extended attributes stay open under the limit; names and xattr values can hold data
ReportCrash writes on the worker's behalf: a crash report outside the container and a CrashReporter plist inside it. Neither held the sentinel in these runs
The deprecated sandbox-exec write-denial profile cannot be combined with App Sandbox: the sandboxed process stops with SIGTRAP before running
Under the zero file-size limit, stdout and stderr must be pipes; a regular-file stderr makes the launcher's own readback fail

Owner condition 2: Container.Do gives each job a fresh, empty folder and, after the worker is reaped on every outcome, sweeps the whole Data tree back to its baseline: added entries and attributes removed, modes restored, immutable flags cleared, symlinks never followed. A sweep that cannot restore the baseline marks the container unclean and refuses further jobs; reports carry counts, never names
All workers signed with one bundle identifier share one container, so jobs on it run one at a time. The owner chose one signed worker copy per concurrency slot for DF-064 cohorts; not implemented

Owner condition 3 evidence: a crash report carries the crashing thread's register values (a known 8-byte pattern in ten registers appeared in the report), so a crash can leak a register set of in-flight data (ten registers checked; arm64 has up to 29 general-purpose registers of 8 bytes); this machine has automatic crash-report submission on. A process whose fatal-signal handler exits first produced no report for either a trap or an abort, with plain crashes reported both before and after.
Owner condition 4: deferred to release qualification by the owner. This machine has no code-signing identity (no Developer ID) and no macOS 13 host

Owner condition 5 evidence: an unprivileged FSEvents stream on the boot volume saw marker writes in /private/tmp, the user temp folder, the home folder and the sandboxed container; it dropped nothing under 20,000 create/delete pairs elsewhere on the volume; a stalled consumer made fseventsd drop events and the observer reported it

Owner condition 3, chosen option (ii) with (iv): the worker's panic hook exits with status 70 at the first panic, printing only the source location. A panic that would abort (one raised during unwinding) then produced no crash report, while a host-sent SIGABRT to the same worker produced one both before and after. Without the hook, the same panic aborted and was reported. Before the hook, a panic in the query task reached the host as INTERNAL failure text that included the panic message, which can hold row values

SEC-001 (security scan, 2026-11-02): the path-based sweep could be redirected outside the container by a process still running in it. The sweep now walks directory handles opened without following symlinks, changes entries only through handles or *at calls that cannot follow, restores a closed directory's permissions by name only with a trailing slash and AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW_ANY (so a hard link or symlink swapped in is refused), opens entries with O_NONBLOCK, checks a baseline entry's inode on root's current device before changing it, and fails closed on what it cannot handle that way or past 64 levels or 131,072 entries
measurement_limits: FSEvents shows that a path changed, not its content or the acting process; flags are merged per path
fseventsd itself records file names on disk; this experiment does not inspect or remove that history
Swap, hibernation and the unified log are not observed
One synthetic 4096-row fixture and one development machine; not the full DF-062 matrix, minimum macOS, signed/installed app or Linux
Kill and crash fire after 15 of 17 source reads; which column chunks those reads carried is not checked
FSEvents watched only the container; an unprivileged volume-wide watch was not tested
Crash reports hold backtraces, not heap, so no sentinel in one is a weak check; reports can leave the machine if analytics sharing is on

ReportCrash stopped writing reports for a process name that had crashed many times (2 misses in about 4 runs with the fixed name 'probe'; 8 of 8 observed after naming each test's executable uniquely). Test apps now use unique names; a production worker with a fixed name would get the same throttling

The volume-wide stream covers the boot volume only, reports paths not processes or contents, and keeps no record of files written and removed between two of its own events on the same path beyond merged flags
Drops did not occur in these load runs; a busier machine could drop, and the observer then fails the observation rather than passing it
Container.Do serializes jobs with an in-process lock; two host processes sharing one container (one bundle identifier) are not serialized, so a cross-process exclusive lock is needed before adoption

ReportCrash writes the in-container CrashReporter plist asynchronously; if it lands between a sweep's walk and its re-check, the container is marked unclean and refuses jobs until it is swept again (an availability limit; the comparison stays strict)
Condition 5's positive controls are direct writes; a delegated write outside the container, such as ReportCrash's report, was not checked through the volume-wide stream
The panic hook covers panics only. Allocation failure, stack overflow and other native faults abort without running it and still produce reports, by the owner's choice
The hook calls std::process::exit, which runs C atexit handlers while other worker threads keep running; a crash during that teardown would still be reported. None was seen
Deployment guidance (iv) relies on administrators setting allowDiagnosticSubmission = false; it stops automatic submission to Apple, not the local report

The hook's location line names the source file; for a panic inside a dependency crate that is the build machine's absolute registry path, including its home folder, unless release builds remap source paths
The handle-based sweep fails closed on a file the worker made unreadable and immutable, and on a baseline file it made unreadable; each marks the container unclean, an availability cost

AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW_ANY (0x0800, from the macOS 27.2 SDK header, which carries no availability note) is verified only on macOS 27.2; on a kernel that rejects it, restoring a closed directory fails and the sweep fails closed. Condition 4's macOS 13 run should cover it
Identity is the inode on root's current device, so a saved baseline stays valid if the volume's device number changes across a reboot; that case was not run
fault_seed_provenance: fault-seeds.json states, per group, which source version each seed ran against; the observations in this folder were regenerated on the final sources
